learning_outcomes.text: Students know and understand the fundamental methods for developing components and systems of the Internet of Things. They can reproduce the essential characteristics of different approaches.

Students have a critical understanding of the most important theories and methods of the Internet of Things. They can apply appropriate platforms, sensors, actuators, wireless and network technologies, and data processing and analysis methods in an application-oriented manner and integrate them into powerful systems.

Students can analyze complex tasks and design suitable IoT solutions. Constraints such as memory, computing time, energy, and networking are analyzed and incorporated into the implementation of the problem solution.

Students use special development tools for data acquisition in sensor nodes and their further processing in distributed IoT systems. They can use their knowledge to solve application-oriented IoT projects.

Students learn to create application-specific requirement catalogs, conceptualize, specify, and then implement an IoT system based on them. Finally, they document and present their results. In this way, they go through all project phases using the example of an application-oriented IoT task.

The development of solutions and the presentation of results is carried out in the form of presentations, thereby strengthening the ability to highlight the essence of a topic in front of an audience and to present it transparently and appealingly.
Students can reflect on future challenges of the Internet of Things under different technical, economic, and ecological framework conditions.

syllabus_topics: Interaction with the real world (sensors, actuators, measurement technology, ...)
assessment_rules: Graded assessment is either an oral examination (duration according to the general examination regulations) or a written project report of approx. 10-15 pages with an associated explanation of approx. 20 minutes. Ungraded assessment is an experimental work, consisting of approx. 6 experiments in total.
